keyword: how long does it take to get to the moon and back to earth

verifications.claim: A round trip to the Moon and back generally takes about 6 to 10 days using conventional spacecraft.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'average travel time... approximately three days'; R2: 'four-day journey to... another four days back... nine and a half days'; R3: '10th day... splashdown'; R4: 'overall mission around the Moon and back expected to take about 10 days'
verifications.reasoning: Sources support one-way ~3-4 days (6-8 total transit) with totals up to 10 days for Artemis, covering the range generally but not precisely for all conventional missions.

verifications.claim: Travel to lunar orbit takes roughly 3 to 4 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately three days'; 'Apollo... around 3 days'; R2: 'roughly a four-day journey to the far side'; R4: 'about four days to reach the Moon'; R7: 'about 3 days'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state 3-4 days for travel to Moon/lunar vicinity using conventional/Apollo/Artemis trajectories.

verifications.claim: Return to Earth from lunar orbit takes roughly 3 to 4 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: Apollo Free Return symmetric ~3 days (implied); R2: 'another four days back to Earth'
verifications.reasoning: Sources indicate return leg mirrors outbound ~3-4 days for Apollo/Artemis free return trajectories.

verifications.claim: Apollo missions averaged roughly 3 days each way.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Apollo missions flew on Free Return transfers. They take around 3 days'; R4: 'fastest Apollo mission (Apollo 8) took 69 hours... slowest (Apollo 17) took 86 hours'; R6: 'nine crewed missions... just over 78 hours (3 days 6 hours)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Apollo one-way times averaging ~3 days (69-86 hours).

verifications.claim: Artemis missions plan for a roughly 10-day round trip.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'nine and a half days'; R3: '10th day... splashdown'; R4: 'overall... about 10 days'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state Artemis II total mission ~10 days, applicable to Artemis missions.

verifications.claim: Apollo 8 reached lunar orbit in 69 hours and 8 minutes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'The fastest Apollo mission (Apollo 8) took 69 hours and 8 minutes to reach the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match in R4 for Apollo 8 time to Moon.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 journey, including lunar surface time, took over 12 days to complete in 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Apollo 17, in December 1972'; R5: 'At 13:24:59... December 19 1972... Apollo 17... launched [Dec 7 implied by context, total >12 days confirmed historically matching sources]'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Apollo 17 in 1972 with total duration over 12 days (launch Dec 7 to splashdown Dec 19).

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission is scheduled to take around 10 days to orbit the Moon and return to Earth.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'will not... go into lunar orbit. Instead... loop around it... nine and a half days'; R3: 'loop behind it... not land... splashdown... April 10'; R4: 'about four days to reach the Moon... 10 days'
verifications.reasoning: Time ~10 days supported, but explicitly not entering lunar orbit (flyby/loop), contradicting 'orbit the Moon'.

verifications.claim: Distance to the Moon is roughly 238,900 miles.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Exact average distance stated as 238,855 miles, roughly 238,900.

verifications.claim: Light takes 1.52 seconds to travel to the Moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Average distance: 1.3 seconds... Closest point: 1.2 seconds Farthest point: 1.4 seconds'
verifications.reasoning: Sources give 1.2-1.4 seconds max, average 1.3; 1.52 contradicts.

verifications.claim: New Horizons robotic probe took ~8 hours to the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'passed the moon in just 8 hours 35 minutes'; R4: '8 hours and 35 minutes'; R6: '8 hours and 35 minutes'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time ~8 hours confirmed across sources.

verifications.claim: Apollo missions took ~3 days to reach the Moon
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately three days... Apollo... around 3 days'; R4: 'average time... about three days'; R6: 'just over 78 hours (3 days 6 hours)'; R7: 'about 3 days'
verifications.reasoning: Consistent statement of ~3 days for Apollo to Moon.
